drivingQuestion: Why should one who vows half his valuation be flogged, and why must he pay the whole?
outcomeNote: The word לוקה is reinterpreted and its ground supplied; nothing further is pressed.

segments.he: לוֹקֶה?! אַמַּאי? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לוֹקֶה בְּעֵרֶךְ שָׁלֵם, מַאי טַעְמָא? גְּזֵירָה ״חֲצִי (עֶרְכִּי) [עֶרְכּוֹ]״ אַטּוּ ״עֵרֶךְ חֶצְיוֹ״, וְעֵרֶךְ חֶצְיוֹ הָוֵי דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Since he did not commit a sin, «why is he flogged? Rav Pappa said» in response: «He is flogged,» i.e., punished, «in» that he must donate his «full valuation. What is the reason» he needs to give his full valuation? A rabbinic «decree» was issued that one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate «half of my valuation,» must give the value of his entire self, «due to» a concern that this case might become confused with the similar one of a person who vows to donate «the valuation of half of himself. And» the halakha in such a case is that he must give the value of his entire self, as «the valuation of half of him is an item upon which the soul is dependent.»
